questions.question_text: What is the primary difference between a 'Layer' and a 'Tier' in software architecture?
questions.explanation: A 'Layer' is a logical separation of concerns within the code (e.g., UI, Business, Data). A 'Tier' is a physical separation of components on different infrastructure (e.g., Client, App Server, DB Server).

options.text: There is no difference; the terms are synonymous.
Layers are logical separations; Tiers are physical deployment separations.
Layers are for databases; Tiers are for user interfaces.

questions.question_text: Which TWO of the following statements about the 'Facade' design pattern are true?
questions.explanation: Facades provide a simplified interface to a complex subsystem, reducing coupling between the client and the subsystem's complex internals.

options.text: It provides a simplified interface to a complex subsystem.
It allows a class to have only one instance.
It reduces coupling between the client and the complex subsystem.
It is used to traverse elements of a collection.

questions.question_text: Determine whether the following are 'Functional Requirements' or 'Constraints'.
questions.explanation: Constraints limit the solution space (budget, legal, technology mandates). Functional requirements describe what the system must do.

rows.text: The system must run on the existing Linux servers.
The user must be able to reset their password via email.
The development budget is capped at $50,000.
The system must generate a monthly sales report.

questions.question_text: In the context of documentation, what does the 'Golden Rule' of arc42 suggest?
questions.explanation: The Golden Rule of documentation is to only document what is relevant and adds value for the stakeholders, avoiding unnecessary work ('write only what is read').

options.text: Document absolutely everything, just in case.
Only document what you really need to communicate; avoid 'write-only' documentation.
Never document anything; the code is the only truth.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are typical 'Quality Scenarios' types?
questions.explanation: Usage scenarios (normal use), Change scenarios (maintenance/evolution), and Failure scenarios (resilience/recovery) are the standard types of quality scenarios.

questions.question_text: Classify the following architectural views as 'Static' or 'Dynamic'.
questions.explanation: The Context View and Building Block View show structure (Static). The Runtime View shows behavior over time (Dynamic).

rows.text: Building Block View
Runtime View
Context View (System Scope)

questions.question_text: What is the core idea of 'Domain-Driven Design' (DDD)?
questions.explanation: DDD focuses on tackling complex software projects by connecting the implementation to an evolving model of the core business concepts (the Domain).

options.text: Aligning the software design closely with the business domain and its logic.

questions.question_text: Which TWO of the following statements about 'Interfaces' are correct?
questions.explanation: Interfaces act as contracts between components, decoupling the implementation from the usage. They should generally be stable and well-defined.

options.text: Interfaces decouple the caller from the implementation.
Interfaces should expose as many implementation details as possible.
Interfaces define the expected behavior and inputs/outputs.
Interfaces increase the coupling between modules.

questions.question_text: Evaluate the following statements regarding 'Technical Debt'.
questions.explanation: Technical debt is a metaphor for the implied cost of additional rework caused by choosing an easy solution now instead of a better approach that would take longer. It needs to be managed and eventually 'paid back'.

rows.text: Technical debt should be completely avoided in every project.
Technical debt can be incurred intentionally to speed up delivery.
Technical debt never needs to be paid back.
Unmanaged technical debt can make future changes significantly harder.

questions.question_text: What is the 'Interface Segregation Principle' (the 'I' in SOLID)?
questions.explanation: Clients should not be forced to depend on interfaces they do not use. It is better to have specific, narrow interfaces than a single general-purpose one.

options.text: A class should implement as many interfaces as possible.
Clients should not be forced to depend on interfaces they do not use.
Interfaces should be segregated into separate files.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are benefits of using 'Design Patterns'?
questions.explanation: Design patterns provide proven solutions to common problems, facilitate communication (shared vocabulary), and improve design flexibility. They do not automatically generate code or guarantee zero bugs.

options.text: They provide proven solutions to common design problems.
They provide a shared vocabulary for developers.
They automatically generate the source code.
They make the design more flexible and maintainable.
They guarantee that the software will be bug-free.

questions.question_text: Decide whether the following concepts relate to 'Security' or 'Safety'.
questions.explanation: Security protects the system from malicious attacks (Confidentiality, Integrity). Safety ensures the system does not harm the environment or people (e.g., ABS brakes, medical devices).

rows.text: Preventing unauthorized access to user data.
Ensuring the medical device does not overheat and burn the patient.
Protecting against SQL injection attacks.
Ensuring the car's airbag deploys correctly in a crash.

questions.question_text: What is the primary role of the 'Presentation Layer' in a Layered Architecture?
questions.explanation: The Presentation Layer (or UI Layer) is responsible for handling user interactions and displaying information. It delegates business logic to the Business Layer.

options.text: To persist data to the database.
To handle user interaction and display information.

questions.question_text: Which TWO of the following are characteristics of 'Microservices'?
questions.explanation: Microservices are independently deployable and organized around business capabilities. They are not necessarily built in the same language (polyglot) and do not share a single massive database (database per service).

options.text: They must all be written in the same programming language.
They are organized around business capabilities.
They all share a single, monolithic database.

questions.question_text: Assign the following diagrams to their UML type: 'Structure Diagram' or 'Behavior Diagram'.
questions.explanation: Class and Deployment diagrams show static structure. Use Case and Sequence diagrams show dynamic behavior.

rows.text: Class Diagram
Use Case Diagram
Deployment Diagram
Sequence Diagram

questions.question_text: In the 'Broker' pattern, what is the role of the 'Stub' (or Proxy)?
questions.explanation: The Stub (or Proxy) resides on the client side and provides a local interface that mimics the remote service, hiding the details of the network communication (marshalling/unmarshalling) from the client.

options.text: To store the data on the server.
To act as a local representative of a remote object, hiding communication details.
To manage the central registry of services.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are typical sections in the 'arc42' documentation template?
questions.explanation: Introduction and Goals, Building Block View, and Runtime View are standard arc42 sections. 'Employee Vacation Plan' and 'Stock Market Ticker' are not.

questions.question_text: Determine if the following statements about 'Loose Coupling' are True or False.
questions.explanation: Loose coupling makes systems easier to maintain and change. It does not mean components don't communicate; it means they communicate via stable abstractions.

rows.text: Loose coupling makes the system more difficult to maintain.
Loose coupling allows components to be changed independently.
Loose coupling means components never exchange data.

questions.question_text: What is the main goal of the 'Singleton' design pattern?
questions.explanation: The Singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance and provides a global point of access to it.

options.text: To create a family of related objects.
To ensure a class has only one instance and provide a global point of access to it.
To decouple an abstraction from its implementation.

questions.question_text: Classify the following statements about 'Architecture Decisions' as True or False.
questions.explanation: Architecture decisions have long-lasting effects and often involve trade-offs. They should be documented (e.g., in ADRs). Reverting them is usually costly.

rows.text: They usually have a high impact on the system structure.
They are easily reversible at any time without cost.
They often involve a trade-off between conflicting quality goals.
They should only be made by the project manager.

questions.question_text: Which design pattern would you use to notify a variable number of objects about a state change in another object?
questions.explanation: The Observer pattern defines a one-to-many dependency so that when one object changes state, all its dependents are notified and updated automatically.

questions.question_text: Which TWO of the following are sub-characteristics of 'Performance Efficiency' in ISO 25010?
questions.explanation: Time Behavior (response time, latency) and Resource Utilization (memory, CPU usage) are key aspects of Performance Efficiency.

questions.question_text: Assign the following examples to the correct interface type: 'Provided Interface' or 'Required Interface'.
questions.explanation: A Provided Interface is what a component offers to others. A Required Interface is what a component needs from others to function.

rows.text: Component A offers a public API method 'calculateTax()'.
Component B calls the 'sendEmail()' method of an external Service C.
Component A implements the 'ISortable' interface.

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of a 'Building Block View' (Whitebox)?
questions.explanation: The Building Block View shows the static decomposition of the system into modules, components, or subsystems and their relationships.

options.text: To show the hardware infrastructure and network topology.
To show the static structure of the system code (modules/components).
To show the sequence of messages between objects at runtime.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are typical 'Cross-cutting Concepts'?
questions.explanation: Internationalization (i18n), Plausibility Checking (Validation), and Transaction Handling are classic cross-cutting concerns that affect many layers and components.

options.text: The main method of the application

questions.question_text: Decide whether the following statements about 'Architecture Patterns' are True or False.
questions.explanation: Patterns are proven solutions to recurring problems. They are not laws; they must be adapted to the specific context.

rows.text: Architecture patterns are reusable solutions to common problems.
You must always implement a pattern exactly as described in the book.
Using patterns facilitates communication among architects.
Patterns automatically guarantee high performance.

questions.question_text: What does the 'S' in SOLID stand for?
questions.explanation: S stands for Single Responsibility Principle: A class should have one, and only one, reason to change.

questions.question_text: Which TWO of the following are benefits of 'Information Hiding'?
questions.explanation: Information hiding reduces dependencies (coupling) because clients rely only on stable interfaces, not internals. This makes the system easier to understand and modify.

options.text: It reduces the dependency of clients on the internal implementation.
It makes the code execute faster.
It improves the understandability of the system by hiding complexity.
It exposes all data fields as public variables.

questions.question_text: Assign the following tasks to the correct role: 'Software Architect' or 'Project Manager'.
questions.explanation: Architects handle technical structure and technology selection. Project Managers handle budget, staffing, and schedules.

rows.text: Selecting the database technology.
Approving the holiday requests of the team.
Defining the layer structure of the application.

questions.question_text: Which UML diagram is best suited to show the physical deployment of artifacts to nodes?
questions.explanation: The Deployment Diagram focuses on the mapping of software artifacts (files, executables) to hardware nodes (servers, devices).

questions.question_text: Which of the following inputs are required for the ATAM (Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method)?
questions.explanation: ATAM requires the Business Goals (to derive drivers), the Architecture (to evaluate), and Stakeholders (to define scenarios). Source code is not the primary input for ATAM.

questions.question_text: Classify the following statements regarding 'Design Principles' as True or False.
questions.explanation: KISS (Keep It Simple, Stupid) and YAGNI (You Ain't Gonna Need It) encourage simplicity and avoiding over-engineering. High coupling is bad.

rows.text: The KISS principle advises to keep solutions as simple as possible.
YAGNI suggests implementing features that might be needed in the far future.
High coupling between modules is a goal of good design.
Separation of Concerns helps to manage complexity.

questions.question_text: What is the relationship between 'Architecture' and 'Design'?
questions.explanation: Architecture deals with high-level structure, fundamental decisions, and cross-cutting concerns. Design deals with the detailed implementation of individual components. Architecture is a subset of design, or design includes architecture.

options.text: Architecture focuses on high-level structure and fundamental decisions; Design includes detailed internal structure.
Architecture is only for hardware; Design is only for software.

questions.question_text: Which TWO of the following patterns are best suited for 'Decoupling' components?
questions.explanation: Observer decouples the subject from observers. Mediator centralizes communication, decoupling colleagues. Singleton often introduces tight coupling to a global instance.

questions.question_text: Identify which of the following are 'Functional' or 'Non-Functional' (Quality) requirements.
questions.explanation: Functional: Calculating values, saving data. Non-functional: Scalability, availability.

rows.text: The system must support 1000 concurrent users.
The system must calculate the interest rate based on the account balance.
The system must be available 99.9% of the time.

questions.question_text: In the context of software architecture, what is a 'Trade-off'?
questions.explanation: A trade-off is a decision where improving one quality attribute (e.g., security) necessitates sacrificing another (e.g., performance or ease of use). There is rarely a perfect solution.

options.text: A compromise between conflicting quality goals or requirements.
A method to swap two modules at runtime.

questions.question_text: Which of the following are standard ways to document software architecture?
questions.explanation: UML diagrams, text descriptions (like arc42), and Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) are standard documentation tools. 'Oral tradition' is not a reliable documentation method.

questions.question_text: Assign the following descriptions to the correct arc42 section.
questions.explanation: Context View (Section 3) shows external neighbors. Building Block View (Section 5) shows internal static structure. Deployment View (Section 7) shows infrastructure.

rows.text: Shows the system as a black box and its external interfaces.
Shows the decomposition of the system into modules and components.
Shows the mapping of software artifacts to hardware nodes.
Describes the static code structure.
